verdict.rationale: Bruno ships its own mock-response serving and environment switching, both selectable at runtime via the environment selector and the CLI's --global-env-var override. Together these let tests target a mock or non-production environment instead of production data. Safe Mode is script-runtime isolation, not data isolation, so it is not credited. missing for 10: documented sandbox/staging environment workflow, explicit guarantees or guards preventing production data access, depth on mock server configuration, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Serve realistic mock responses while you build.
adding search filter to environment selector dropdown
add --global-env-var to override global environment variables at runtime
